Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

nmpilot (development version)

  • nm_suggest_model(): the combined residual error model is now retained only when its BIC is better by more than 15 (10 before; point E28). The threshold was chosen with the simulation validation (inst/validation/validate_suggest_model.R, 8 scenarios, rich designs): correct error model 87% on average over the three true error models, as with 10, with the proportional model found more often (86% vs 82%), the additive model as often (85%) and the combined model a little less often (90% vs 95%); 20 replicates per scenario, one combined-error scenario. In sparse designs no BIC is computed and the threshold plays no role.

  • New function nm_check_dataset() (point B5): checks that a dataset can be read by NONMEM (ID, TIME and DV columns; missing ID or TIME; non-numeric values; decreasing times within a subject, except at reset records; inconsistent EVID, MDV and AMT; duplicated records or observations; negative DV and outliers compared with the observations taken at the same time after dose). It reads the file as NONMEM does and only reports: the data are never modified. Listed in the task guide (stage 1).

  • Output files are named output_file everywhere (point B11): in nm_write_ctl(), nm_ctl_mu(), nm_ctl_iov(), nm_ctl_m3(), nm_export_data(), nm_export_plot() and nm_guide() (formerly file), nm_add_rate() and nm_convert_ctl() (formerly out_file), nm_gof() (formerly docx_file), nm_extract_run_table() (formerly output_name) and nm_vpc() (formerly plot_file). The former names are still accepted, with a warning, until version 1.0. overwrite was already used everywhere.

  • Every figure written by the package goes through nm_export_plot() (point B9): nm_gof(save_docx = TRUE) no longer calls ggsave() directly. Formats: .jpg, .png, .pdf and .tiff, chosen from the extension.

nmpilot 0.9.0

  • Task guide (nm_guide()): every argument of the code examples is explained by a comment at the end of its line, and nm_model_diagram() is listed as available, with an example. New test test-guide.R: every function and every argument cited by the examples must exist (a former argument name, accepted with a warning, is reported), and every example must parse.

  • Automatic checks on GitHub (point A.14): R CMD check runs at each push on Windows, macOS and Linux (current R), and on Linux with R-devel and the previous R; test coverage is measured with covr and sent to Codecov. Badges in the README.

  • Documentation website (point A.13): https://nskoch.github.io/nmpilot/, built with pkgdown and published at each push: the README and the task guide on the home page, the functions grouped by stage of the analysis, the vignettes and this file. Its address is in DESCRIPTION.

  • One reader for the records $INPUT, $THETA, $OMEGA and $SIGMA (point A.11, third part), shared by nm_ctl_check(), the transformations, nm_identify_parameters(), nm_convert_ctl() and nm_profile(), which had each their own (new internal file R/nm_ctl_read.R). Results are unchanged on the 186 control streams of the comparison corpus, except for the following corrections:

    • $THETA: all the $THETA records are read by the check of the transformations (only the first one before); (0.5 FIX), with FIX inside the parentheses, and (0 1 5), with blanks as separators, are read; (2.0)X8 gives 8 THETAs; $THETAP and $THETAPV (priors) are no longer counted as THETAs by nm_profile();
    • $OMEGA/$SIGMA: FIX anywhere in a BLOCK(n) record fixes the whole block, as in NONMEM (only when FIX was on every line before); the label of an ETA of a BLOCK is the comment of the line of its variance (one value per line gave shifted labels); a comment-only line is no longer a label; BLOCK(1) SAME no longer swallows the values of the next record (one ETA was lost); new column omega_comment (full comment);
    • $INPUT: DROP written alone is not a data item;
    • nm_convert_ctl(): a name assigned after IF(...), assigned as an array element (MTIME(1) = ...) or assigned in an earlier model record ($PK before $DES or $ERROR) is no longer replaced by THETA(n)/ETA(n); control streams already in standard NONMEM syntax are left unchanged. Tests in test-ctl-read.R.

  • Print and plot methods harmonised (point A.11, second part):

    • every plot() method returns the figure (a ggplot, or a patchwork for the combined panels of nm_gof), shown when not assigned and ready for nm_export_plot(). plot.nm_gof() and plot.nm_model_diagram() printed the figure themselves and returned the object;
    • the argument that chooses the figure is type in every method: plot.nm_compare() and plot.nm_gof() (formerly which), plot.nm_optimize_base() (formerly area); the former names still work until 1.0, with a warning;
    • the run log of nm_run() and nm_vpc_ctl() has the class nm_run_log, the result of nm_extract_run_table() the class nm_run_table, and the result of nm_data_previsual() the class nm_data_previsual, each with a print method giving a short summary. They remain a data frame or a list: existing code that uses their columns or elements is unchanged.

  • Argument names harmonised before version 1.0 (point A.11, first part). The former names and forms still work until 1.0, with a warning that gives the new one:

    • the control stream is ctl everywhere: nm_run(ctl, nmfe_path, ...) (formerly ctl_files, after nmfe_path), nm_profile(ctl, nmfe_path, ...) (formerly ctl_path, after nmfe_path), nm_identify_parameters(ctl) (formerly file), nm_convert_ctl(ctl) (formerly ctl_file). The former order, with nmfe_path first, is recognised when the arguments are given by position;
    • a finished run is given by its path, run (control stream, run directory or stem): nm_vpc(run, ...) and nm_vpc_ctl(run, ...) (formerly run_name + analysis_dir), nm_extract_run_table(run) (formerly run_rep + run_name, or run_path);
    • the output directory is output_dir: nm_bootstrap() (formerly run_dir), nm_derivatives_ctl() and nm_data_previsual() (formerly out_dir);
    • nm_profile() takes verbose (formerly quiet, the opposite), and nm_bootstrap() strip_tables (formerly strip_table), as the other functions. The README, the vignettes, the guide and the tests use the new names. Tests in test-deprecated-args.R.

  • New function nm_model_diagram() (point A.7): tree of the models tested in a project. Each run is linked to the run it was derived from, read in its control stream as a comment with the PsN and Pirana convention (;; 1. Based on: run3, or ;; Based on: 3 for run3) or given with parents =, which also corrects or removes links. Each run shows its OFV, its dOFV and its change in the number of estimated parameters relative to its parent, coloured by convergence state (covariance done, no covariance, not converged, not completed, simulation). Returns the table of the tree and a ggplot2 figure, which nm_export_plot() saves. Circular links and parents absent from the project are reported. Tests in test-model-diagram.R.

Reading of real outputs of NONMEM 7.1 to 7.6 (point A.3): a sample of 43 runs (7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 7.4.1, 7.6, and a few NONMEM V/VI outputs; models with and without $DES, ADVAN1 to ADVAN13) was read with nm_extract_runs(); the following problems were found and fixed. NONMEM 7.5 was not checked (no output of this version was available).

  • nm_extract_runs() failed for a whole directory (“subscript out of bounds”) when a run without .ext had 10 ETAs or more: from the 10th element on, NONMEM prints the rows of the matrices as ET10, EP10, which were not recognised. These labels are now read, and a correlation whose variance is missing is reported as NA instead of stopping nm_extract_runs() and nm_extract_run_table().

  • A simulation-only run of NONMEM 7.1, which prints an empty #METH: line, was reported as interrupted; it is now reported as a simulation.

  • nm_ctl_check() reads the use of THETA(n), ETA(n), EPS(n), CMT, EVID, MDV and RATE in the code records only: an initial estimate such as $THETA (18.3 FIXED) was taken for a use of THETA(18) (“used but not declared”), and a title such as $PROBLEM ... 1 CMT for a use of CMT. With PREDPP ($SUBROUTINES), EVID and MDV used in the code without being in $INPUT are no longer reported, as NM-TRAN supplies these items. RATE with KA is no longer reported when a zero-order input into any compartment (D2, R3…) is modelled.

  • NONMEM V/VI outputs: the tables printed in the .lst were read as parameter estimates, and the OFV, printed about ten lines below its banner, was not found. Both are now read.

  • nm_extract_runs() reads the number of observations (n_obs) in the .lst (“TOT. NO. OF OBS RECS”) when there is no .smr, which is the case of the runs launched with nm_run() or nmfe without Wings for NONMEM; the BIC is then computed as well. On the 43 runs of the sample, the value read in the .lst equals the one of the .smr whenever both exist.

  • nm_extract_run_table() no longer requires a .ext file: when it is missing or holds no estimates (empty file), the estimates printed in the .lst are used, as in nm_extract_runs(), and the table footer says so. This covers the runs of older NONMEM versions or of PsN without .ext (16 of the 43 runs of the sample have none). The .lst prints three significant digits: on three runs read both ways, the estimates differ by less than 0.4 % and the OFV is the same.

  • A model written with $DES (the example run2 rewritten with ADVAN13) was run with NONMEM 7.6 through the whole chain: estimation (same OFV and estimates as run2), nm_extract_runs(), nm_extract_run_table(), nm_vpc_ctl() and nm_vpc(), nm_profile(), nm_bootstrap() and the derivatives run of nm_derivatives_ctl().

  • Control streams written by nm_write_ctl(), nm_ctl_mu(), nm_ctl_iov() and nm_ctl_m3() were run through NONMEM 7.6 (75 runs: every structure, error model, estimation method and transformation; action 26). Six errors were found and fixed:

    • $DES models (ADVAN13, ADVAN6) are written with TOL=9, required by NM-TRAN (error 145);
    • FO is written METHOD=ZERO instead of METHOD=FO (error 287);
    • nm_ctl_m3() adds M3LLOQ, M3SD, M3PBQL before the options of $TABLE, not after FILE= (error 20);
    • nm_ctl_m3() writes both definitions of Y in one IF/THEN/ELSE block, the M3 quantities being computed before it. The former code defined Y with the residual error in a block written IF (BQL.EQ.0.OR.ICALL.EQ.4) THEN, which NM-TRAN 7.6 refused (error 122, “EPS VARIABLES REQUIRED WITH POPULATION DATA”, and warning 53): a block testing ICALL.EQ.4 is simulation code for NM-TRAN. The censoring flag M3CENS keeps the test of ICALL out of the blocks defining Y. The four M3 control streams then ran with NONMEM 7.6 (estimation with LAPLACE converged, covariance step completed);
    • nm_ctl_mu(mode = "linear") writes 0.0001 instead of log(1) = 0 for a THETA whose initial value is 1 (error 260: initial estimate of 0);
    • three-compartment models with first-order absorption (ADVAN12): the default initial values of the second peripheral compartment are now Q4 = 2 and V4 = 400 (they were equal to Q3 and V3, which PREDPP refuses: “K32, OR K42 IS TOO CLOSE TO AN EIGENVALUE”).

  • nm_ctl_check() reports these NM-TRAN errors: TOL missing with a general ADVAN, unknown METHOD, THETA initial estimate of 0 not fixed, $TABLE item written after the options, Y with EPS/ERR defined only in IF blocks testing ICALL.EQ.4. No false alarm on the 38 real control streams of the sample nor on the example project.

  • New tests for these cases and for models written with $DES (test-lst-versions.R, test-des.R, test-nmtran-errors.R), built from the example run or written by hand.

  • Tests on control streams and outputs not written by nmpilot (point A.4): seven runs of the package bbr (Metrum Research Group, MIT licence; NONMEM 7.4.4) are copied in tests/testthat/fixtures/public/bbr, with their licence and source. They cover $DES, $PRIOR, MTIME, BAYES, a FOCEI > BAYES > IMP chain, $SIMULATION ONLYSIM, $ABBR REPLACE with 62 ETAs and $MIX. The new tests check nm_ctl_check(), nm_identify_parameters(), the reading of the .lst, nm_extract_runs() and nm_convert_ctl() on these files. They showed six problems, fixed:

    • nm_ctl_check() reported as an error $TABLE items written on a line below the options, which NM-TRAN accepts; only an item written after an option of the same line is reported now.
    • $ABBR REPLACE with a range (ETA(OCC_CL)=ETA(,3:32), also ETA(3 TO 32 BY 2)): the ETAs were reported as unused by nm_ctl_check() and not linked to their parameter by nm_identify_parameters(). The names given by $ABBR REPLACE (ranges and lists) are now replaced by their elements, so that IOV ETAs are linked to their parameter. nm_identify_parameters() also counts the ETAs of $OMEGA BLOCK(n) SAME(k) (k blocks, not one).
    • Shrinkage read in the .lst: beyond 10 ETAs, the values continued on the following lines were ignored (20 values read out of 62).
    • Without .ext, the OMEGA matrix of the .lst was misread beyond 12 ETAs (rows wrapped by NONMEM): 12 variances read out of 62.
    • nm_identify_parameters(): a covariate effect written in a helper variable added on the log scale (CLEGFR = LOG(EGFR/90)*THETA(6), CL = EXP(THETA(3) + CLEGFR + ETA(3))) was taken for a typical value.
    • nm_identify_parameters(): a THETA present in every branch of a conditional definition (IF(PATIENT.EQ.0) KOUT = EXP(THETA(1) + ETA(1)), IF(PATIENT.EQ.1) KOUT = EXP(THETA(1) + ETA(2))) was taken for a covariate effect; it is the typical value. The THETAs of MTIME(n) and of the mixture probabilities P(n) of $MIX are returned in the new element special_theta instead of unmapped_theta.

nmpilot 0.8.1

  • Linux and macOS: nm_bootstrap() no longer depends on cmd.exe. Its sequential loop (n_cores = 1) now uses the launcher shared by nm_run(), nm_profile() and nm_jackknife(), which calls cmd.exe on Windows and the nmfe script directly on Linux and macOS. On these systems, a launcher that is not executable is reported with a clear message (“chmod +x”) instead of a failure of the system call. The documentation of nmfe_path gives a Linux example. Checked on Linux with a simulated nmfe for nm_run(), nm_profile(), nm_jackknife(), nm_bootstrap(), nm_vpc_ctl() and nm_vpc(), one run at a time and in parallel; not yet with a real NONMEM installation on Linux or macOS.

nmpilot 0.8.0

  • The package is renamed nmpilot (formerly nmtools), to avoid confusion with an unrelated GitHub repository of the same name in the same field. Install it with remotes::install_github("nskoch/nmpilot") and load it with library(nmpilot); remove the old package with remove.packages("nmtools"). No function is renamed.
  • The options are renamed nmpilot.n_cores and nmpilot.warn_synced (formerly nmtools.n_cores and nmtools.warn_synced).
  • The files written by parallel runs are renamed <run>_nmpilot.bat (or .sh), <run>_nmpilot.log, <run>_nmpilot.err and <run>.nmpilot_done. Files left by earlier versions (*_nmtools.*, *.nmtools_done) are not used and can be deleted.
  • nm_vpc_ctl() wrote FIX on every row of the $OMEGA and $SIGMA blocks of the _orig and _sim control streams, which NM-TRAN refuses (error 52, “THIS OPTION HAS ALREADY BEEN SPECIFIED”): FIX is now written once, on the BLOCK(n) line. Found with NONMEM 7.6 on the example project.
  • nm_vpc(): when a time bin between two others was empty, the bins after it were drawn at the wrong time (the midpoint of a bin was looked up by position instead of by bin number) and the last bin was dropped, with the warning “Removed 1 row containing missing values (geom_line)”. On the example project with automatic bins, the statistics of the 12 h bin were drawn at 24 h and the 24 h bin was missing. Fixed.
  • nm_vpc(): the first line of the .fit tables was always skipped, as if it were a header, whereas nm_vpc_ctl() writes them without header (NOHEADER): when a data set starts with an observation, that observation was lost. Header lines (“TABLE NO.”, column names) are now recognised and left out, and no record is skipped.
  • nm_run() (and the functions that launch runs through it, such as nm_vpc_ctl()): a simulation-only run ($SIMULATION ONLYSIM, e.g. the _sim run of a VPC) that finished is now reported with minimization_status = "simulation" and run_ok = TRUE, and is skipped as done by skip_terminated = TRUE. It was reported with NA and relaunched at each call.
  • nm_extract_runs(): a simulation-only run ($SIMULATION ONLYSIM) that finished is now reported with run_state = "simulation", min_status = "SIMULATION" and min_ok = NA; it was reported as "interrupted" with min_ok = FALSE. The subproblems of a run (SUBPROBLEMS=n) are no longer counted as problems in n_problems (the _sim run of a 500-replicate VPC had n_problems = 501).
  • The entries below, up to 0.7.1, were released under the name nmtools.

nmpilot 0.7.1

  • No change in the code. This release is the first to contain the work of versions 0.6.0 (parallel NONMEM runs) and 0.7.0 (reading NONMEM outputs), described below. By mistake, the GitHub releases v0.6.0 and v0.7.0 (and their Zenodo archives) were made on the commit of version 0.5.0: they hold the code of 0.5.0. Use 0.7.1 or later.

nmpilot 0.7.0

Reading NONMEM outputs: several $EST and $PROB, IOV, $MIX, failed runs

  • With several $EST records (for example ITS > SAEM > IMP > BAYES > FOCEI), the OFV, the minimisation status, the shrinkage and the covariance step are now those of the last estimation step; they came from the first steps. New column est_methods in nm_extract_runs() (e.g. "ITS > SAEM > IMP(eval) > BAYES > FOCEI") and n_est. EM and Bayesian status lines (“STOCHASTIC PORTION WAS COMPLETED”, “EXPECTATION ONLY PROCESS COMPLETED”, “OPTIMIZATION WAS NOT TESTED”) are recognised.
  • The same rule is applied in nm_run(), nm_profile(), nm_bootstrap(), nm_jackknife() (OFV, status and THETA of the last step) and nm_compare() (OFV).
  • nm_run(): the covariance status is read from the status lines only; the sentence “AFTER CHECKING THAT THE COVARIANCE STEP PRODUCES REASONABLE OUTPUT”, printed after “HOWEVER, PROBLEMS OCCURRED”, made runs whose covariance step had succeeded appear as "min_success_cov_failed".
  • With several $PROB, the last problem that has an estimation is read (a simulation problem after the estimation is skipped); new column n_problems.
  • nm_extract_runs(): when the .ext is empty, has no final row, or gives an OFV different from the .lst (an .ext left by another run with the same name), the estimates and standard errors are read in the .lst, with a warning and “EXT/LST MISMATCH” in warnings; new column params_source ("ext", "lst" or "smr").
  • New column run_state: "completed", "interrupted" (the output stops before the end of the last step), "terminated" (PROGRAM TERMINATED) or "nmtran_error". A run that is not completed has min_ok = FALSE.
  • IOV: ETAs declared by $OMEGA ... SAME (also BLOC(n), SAME(k)) are marked in $params (new column same) and counted in n_eta_same.
  • n_omega and n_sigma now count the estimated elements only (not FIX, not SAME, not the zeros outside the blocks): on the example project, 3 and 0 instead of 6 and 1. ETAs fixed to 0 are left out of max_eta_shrink.
  • $MIX: new columns mix, n_subpop and mix_assign (subjects per subpopulation, from the .phm); new element $mixture (probability of each subpopulation for each subject); mixing-proportion THETAs without another name are named MIX_P; the shrinkage of an ETA is its smallest value over the subpopulations (NONMEM prints 100 % in the subpopulations that do not use it). nm_filter_runs() filters $mixture too.
  • Run files are matched without regard to case (NONMEM 7.1 wrote RUN.EXT next to run.lst), and .mod control streams are recognised.
  • Checked on 11 real runs (NONMEM 7.1 to 7.4): chains of five $EST, SAEM > IMP, ITS > FOCE, IOV, $MIX with METHOD=1 and CONDITIONAL, empty .ext, .ext from another run.

nmpilot 0.6.0

Parallel NONMEM runs

  • New argument n_cores in nm_run(), nm_profile(), nm_jackknife(), nm_bootstrap(), nm_vpc_ctl() and nm_suggest_run() (default 1: runs one after the other, as before). With n_cores > 1, each run is started in the background from its own directory (NM-TRAN writes its work files in the current directory) and at most n_cores runs go on at the same time. n_cores = "auto" uses the physical cores minus one; n_cores = "ask" shows the cores and asks the number once per R session (the answer is kept in options(nmtools.n_cores); set it to NULL to ask again).
  • New nm_cores(): logical and physical cores of the computer, and the number of runs "auto" would use.
  • Each parallel run writes the console output of nmfe to <run>_nmtools.log (and <run>_nmtools.err). If R is interrupted, the runs already started go on in the background and are listed.
  • nm_run(): with n_cores > 1, several control streams in a flat layout (shared folder) are run one after the other, with a warning. nm_jackknife() now always runs each jackknife data set in its own subdirectory jk_run/<name>/. nm_bootstrap() uses working subdirectories slot1, slot2, …
  • Checked with NONMEM 7.6 on Windows with 5 runs at a time: nm_run() (4 runs), nm_profile() (12 grid values), nm_jackknife() (60 runs) and nm_bootstrap() (20 replicates), all successful. On Windows the launcher calls nmfe without any redirection inside the batch file: a 2>&1 there keeps the first 2>trash.tmp of nmfe in force and the compilation fails.

Display fixes

  • nm_profile(): the start message gives the initial value of the profiled THETA and, when the .ext of the control stream exists, its final estimate (it showed only the initial value, as “current value”).
  • print.nm_jackknife(): the reference OFV is printed with three decimals (it was rounded to four significant digits, e.g. -1224).

nmpilot 0.5.0

Direct comparison of two models (nm_compare())

  • Vuong (1989) and Clarke (2007) tests on the individual contributions to the objective function (iOFV of the .phi files), for non-nested models fitted to the same data, without correction and with AIC-like and BIC-like corrections for the number of parameters (read from the .ext files, or given with n_par). Likelihood ratio test when nested = TRUE.
  • Subject bootstrap of the delta iOFV (no re-estimation): confidence interval of dOFV and probability that run 2 has a lower OFV (and AIC). Influence: number of subjects, largest contributions first, whose removal reverses the sign of dOFV.
  • Delta iOFV versus covariates (covariates =, Spearman or Kruskal-Wallis with Bonferroni adjustment); parameters of the two runs matched by name (estimate, SE, RSE, shrinkage, ratio) and paired EBEs.
  • New plots: "gain_map" (|CWRES_2| - |CWRES_1| versus TIME and PRED, loess with a 95% subject-bootstrap band), "overlay_gof" (diagnostics of both runs superimposed), "bootstrap", "iofv_covariate", "parameters", "eta_scatter".
  • New summary() method: decision criteria (OFV, AIC, BIC, tests, bootstrap, influence, residual metrics, maximum RSE, condition number from the .cor file, maximum shrinkage, run status) with the run favoured by each.

Improving a base model without iterative runs

  • New nm_derivatives_ctl(): writes an evaluation run of a base model (final estimates fixed, MAXEVAL=0) that tabulates the derivatives of Y with respect to the ETAs, the EPSs and their cross derivatives (verbatim code at the end of $ERROR/$PRED, as PsN linearize). Checked with NONMEM 7.6.
  • New nm_optimize_base(): level 1 from the outputs of the base run (resmod-like models on CWRES, EBE shrinkage, skewness and correlations, ETA-covariate screening); level 2 on the linearized model built from the derivatives table, each candidate re-estimated in R: residual error models, OMEGA blocks, removal of an ETA, inter-occasion variability, covariates on the ETAs (univariate tests, forward inclusion and backward elimination), then the combined proposal. The default objective (objective = "focei") is NONMEM’s FOCE with interaction (modes of the full individual objective, residual-variance term in the determinant) and reproduces the OFV of the base run at its estimates; objective = "fast" is a quicker approximation. plot() shows the dOFV of each candidate as better, no significant change or worse.

Other changes

  • nm_run() reads the OFV and status of an evaluation run (MAXEVAL=0, status "evaluation"), and warns when the analysis directory is inside a folder synchronised by a cloud client (Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive, iCloud, Box), whose client can lock files during compilation (silence with options(nmtools.warn_synced = FALSE)).

nmpilot 0.4.1

  • nm_suggest_model(): the residual error model is chosen on a common structural fit of each interval (iteratively reweighted least squares under a combined variance); the additive, proportional and combined variance models are then compared by BIC on the same leverage-corrected (PRESS) residuals, so that they are nested. Points of leverage above 0.7 and predictions below twice the LLOQ are left out, and the combined model is kept only when its BIC is better by more than 10. On simulated rich data (20 replicates per scenario), the error model is recovered in 60 to 100% of the datasets; better than 0.4.0 for Michaelis-Menten, additive and combined error, lower for some proportional-error scenarios (inst/validation/validate_suggest_model.R).

nmpilot 0.4.0

Data-driven suggestion of structural models

  • New nm_suggest_model(): analyses a NONMEM dataset, rich or sparse, without running NONMEM and ranks candidate models: number of compartments (sums of exponentials compared by BIC), input (IV bolus or infusion, first-order, first-order with lag time, zero-order duration, transit compartments; full-profile fits with a censoring penalty for early BLQ samples), elimination (dose proportionality and curvature of the log-concentration decline) and residual error model (additive, proportional or combined; extended least squares on leverage-corrected residuals). Each candidate comes with initial values for THETA, IIV (variance of individual estimates) and SIGMA, the parameters likely to be hard to estimate and their reasons, and alerts on features outside the tested structures (double peaks, clearance changing between first dose and steady state, unexpected accumulation, less than dose-proportional exposure). Sparse data are analysed as naive pooled data. print() and plot() methods ("profiles", "support", "pooled", "design").
  • New nm_suggest_design(): expected RSE and eta-shrinkage of a candidate for the sampling design of the dataset or another one (population Fisher information matrix, first-order approximation, analytic solution with superposition of doses).
  • New nm_suggest_run(): writes the control streams of the best candidates, runs them with nm_run() and compares the BIC ranking with the data-driven score.
  • New nm_suggest_covariates(): Wasserstein-distance screening of covariates on the individual estimates (CL, central volume, absorption) before any modelling.
  • nm_suggest_run() gives each candidate a dataset that matches its compartment numbering (depot 1 and central 2 for first-order and transit absorption; central 1 for IV and zero-order input, with RATE = -2 on the doses for a modelled duration). A copy is written only when the original dataset does not match; the original file is never modified. With overwrite = TRUE, the candidates are run again even when previous runs of the same name have terminated.
  • nm_write_ctl(): new arguments from and candidate to write the control stream of a candidate of nm_suggest_model(); explicit arguments keep priority. New argument conc_factor: the scale is written S = V/conc_factor (e.g. 1000 for doses in mg, volumes in L and DV in ng/mL); with from, the dose_conc_factor of the suggestion is used.
  • New validation script inst/validation/validate_suggest_model.R (recognition rate of the true structure on simulated datasets).

nmpilot 0.3.0

Writing control streams

Functions ported from the Shiny application “Générateur NONMEM .ctl” (https://nicolas-simon.shinyapps.io/nonmem_ctl_publi/). All return an nm_ctl object (control stream lines, printed as text) and can write a file.

  • New nm_write_ctl(): writes a control stream for a 1- to 3-compartment PK model, IV or extravascular, with first-order, zero-order (modelled rate R1 = K0, RATE = -1, or modelled duration D1, RATE = -2) or transit-compartment absorption, linear or Michaelis-Menten elimination, analytic (ADVAN/TRANS) or ODE solution. $INPUT follows the column order of the dataset; THETA bounds and FIX, IIV as CV% or variance, diagonal or block $OMEGA, additive, proportional or combined error, nine estimation methods, xpose-style sdtab/patab/cotab tables.
  • New nm_ctl_mu(): MU referencing of log-normal parameters ("readable" or "linear" mode).
  • New nm_ctl_iov(): inter-occasion variability with $ABBR REPLACE and $OMEGA BLOCK(p) SAME(n-1); optional check of the occasion column.
  • New nm_ctl_m3(): M3 method for BQL data, with the LLOQ given as a constant, a dataset column, or by analytical method code.
  • New nm_ctl_check(): static check of a control stream (THETA/ETA/EPS used but not declared, over all records including BLOCK, SAME and $ABBR REPLACE; $INPUT items; M3 requirements), with optional line differences from a reference control stream.

nmpilot 0.2.3

  • New nm_jackknife(): leave-one-subject-out jackknife of a NONMEM model (method of the standalone script nonmem-jackknife-influence, doi:10.5281/zenodo.22257994). Ranks the subjects by their likelihood influence |dOFV| and reports the relative THETA shifts (L2 norm, maximum, SE-standardised norm); print() and plot() methods ("bar", "rank", "scatter"). Resumes an interrupted analysis. Data lines are copied verbatim, as in nm_bootstrap().
  • nm_identify_parameters(): new column derived_from in parameter_table, naming the parameters a derived parameter is computed from ("V" for S2 = V, "CL, V" for KE = CL/V; NA otherwise).
  • nm_extract_runs(): covariate-effect and residual-error THETAs are named from their $THETA comment label when it is a short name (CL_WT, PROP, RUV_A, 4 Prop (...) -> Prop) instead of THETA4, THETA5…

nmpilot 0.2.2

Breaking changes

  • Output column names are now in English. nm_extract_run_table(), params table: Parameter, Estimate, RSE_pct, CI95, CI95_lower, CI95_upper (were Parametre, Estimation, RSE_pourcent, IC95, IC95_lower, IC95_upper). nm_summary() and nm_data_previsual(): unique_doses (was doses_uniques).

Wings for NONMEM is optional

  • nm_run(): new argument run_subdir. ".reg" (default) keeps the Wings-compatible layout run1.reg/; any other suffix can be used; "" runs NONMEM in the folder of the control stream, without copying it. A control stream in Wings label syntax cannot be run with run_subdir = "" (clear error message).
  • nm_run(): a relative $DATA path is looked up from the folder of the control stream ($DATA data.csv), then from the run directory ($DATA ../data.csv, Wings style).
  • nm_vpc_ctl(), nm_vpc() and nm_extract_run_table() find a run in <run>.reg/, <run>.nm7/, a folder named <run>, or directly in the analysis directory. nm_vpc_ctl() gains run_subdir; by default the VPC runs use the layout of the estimation run.

Bug fixes

  • nm_run(): NONMEM is now launched from the run directory (NM-TRAN failed when started from another working directory).
  • nm_run(): standard control streams with comments after $THETA or $OMEGA values are no longer taken for Wings control streams.
  • nm_run(): verbose = FALSE now silences all messages.

Documentation

  • Example project in inst/extdata/example: simulated data (60 fictitious subjects, one-compartment oral model) and the NONMEM outputs of a BASE and a FINAL model.
  • Two vignettes: vignette("nmtools") (getting started) and vignette("wasserstein").
  • citation("nmtools") cites the package and, for nm_wasserstein(), the original article.

nmpilot 0.2.1

  • nm_wasserstein(): new argument continuous = "pairwise" to compare every pair of quartiles of a continuous covariate (6 comparisons), as in the pairwise analysis of the original article; Bonferroni-adjusted p-values p_W_adj and p_t_adj are added to the results. The default ("extremes", Q4 vs Q1) is unchanged.
  • nm_identify_parameters(): a THETA assigned under an IF condition whose other branch is a plain constant (e.g. IF (CT01.EQ.1) FALL = THETA(7), ELSE FALL = 1) is now a covariate effect; a covariate term added inside a sum written with extra parentheses (e.g. ((THETA(1)*FALL) + (THETA(8)*(CLCR/89)))) is now a covariate effect.

nmpilot 0.2.0

  • New nm_wasserstein(): distribution-based covariate assessment with the Wasserstein distance (Simon, Hulot and von Fabeck, Front Pharmacol 2026, doi:10.3389/fphar.2026.1804989). For one or several runs, compares the distribution of an ETA between groups of subjects defined by covariates (permutation test on the 1-Wasserstein distance, with a t-test for reference) and reports a Wasserstein-based R2 with the eta-shrinkage. print() and plot() methods (ECDF by group, R2W bar chart).

nmpilot 0.1.0

First public release.

  • Data sets: nm_read_csv(), nm_data_previsual(), nm_plot_dv(), nm_summary(), nm_add_rate(), nm_export_data().
  • Running NONMEM: nm_run(), nm_convert_ctl() (Wings extended control streams).
  • Results: nm_extract_runs(), nm_filter_runs(), nm_compare_runs(), nm_extract_run_table().
  • Parameter identification from the model code: nm_identify_parameters(), nm_identify_directory().
  • Diagnostics: nm_gof(), nm_compare(), nm_vpc_ctl(), nm_vpc().
  • Uncertainty: nm_profile(), nm_bootstrap().
  • Figures: nm_export_plot().
